packageRules.description: Pin every GitHub Action to a full commit SHA. A tag is mutable: whoever can move `v4` can run their code inside a workflow holding GHCR push credentials, sibling PATs and deploy access. Scoped to github-actions on purpose -- pinning Docker tags too would freeze the `:latest` the engine deploy moves by hand.
Group patch and digest updates together

One PR per major. Sharing a branch means a single package whose peer ranges have not caught up blocks every other major behind the same failed install, and a batch of breaking changes cannot be reviewed, merged or reverted one at a time.

vitest and its @vitest/* companions pin each other through exact peer ranges, so a lone major for one of them installs against a core that does not support it and the PR can never go green. They release in lockstep, so they take one branch. Deliberate exception to the rule above, and it has to sit below that rule to win.

typescript-eslint and its @typescript-eslint/* packages peer-require each other on a matching major, so a lone major for one of them can never install: the eslint-plugin PR asks for a parser major that is still on the old one, and the parser PR fails the mirror image of the same conflict. Five of these sat red for 28 days across activepieces-beliq, beliq-cli and beliq-mcp, each blocked on a sibling PR that was itself blocked. They release in lockstep, so they take one branch. Same exception as vitest above, and it has to sit below the one-PR-per-major rule to win.

astro and its @astrojs/* integrations move together: the integration reaches Astro's markdown renderer as a transitive dependency of `astro` itself, so bumping the integration alone leaves the old renderer in the tree. @astrojs/mdx 8 on astro 7 fails the build with "`@astrojs/markdown-satteri` is too old to render `.mdx` files", and Astro's own message notes that a caret range on the older version will not pick it up. Same lockstep exception as vitest and typescript-eslint above.

typescript-eslint peers typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0 and throws `typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0` when it loads, so a typescript 7 update cannot lint in any repo that uses it and the PR can never go green. Ten were open across both owners. Lift when typescript-eslint ships TS >=7.1 support; https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/issues/10940 tracks it. A repo that does not use typescript-eslint overrides this in its own renovate.json.

customManagers.description: Seven release workflows pin the npm CLI itself with `npm install -g npm@<version>`, so a publish cannot silently move to a newly released npm. No built-in manager reads a version inside a `run:` line, so without this manager the pin freezes on the day it was typed. Proven 2026-09-22 by running Renovate against a copy of beliq-cli with the pin lowered to 11.5.1: it extracted zero dependencies named npm, and only after the marker comment and this manager were added did it propose 11.19.1 and 12.0.2. The marker comment above each site is what makes the line readable, and `scripts/check-custom-managers.mjs` in this repo fails when a claimed workflow carries a marker the regex cannot read, or an `npm install -g npm@` line carries no marker. The built-in `customManagers:githubActionsVersions` preset does not cover this shape: it only reads `<NAME>_VERSION:` environment variables. `astral-sh/setup-uv`'s `version:` input needs no marker, because the `github-actions` manager already extracts it as a `uses-with` dependency. Scoped to `ci.yml` and `release.yml` rather than every workflow so it does not also claim beliq-validate-action's `.github/workflows/test-action.yml`, whose pin that repo's own custom manager owns: a preset manager and a repo manager both apply, so an overlapping file pattern reads the same line twice. npm majors arrive as their own PR under the one-PR-per-major rule above, and merging one means checking npm's `engines` against each workflow's `node-version`: npm 12.0.2 requires node `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`.
